A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching algorithms, main theorems, Figure 1, Table 1, and Appendices A–D. The text, equations, and visual material support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 7 reports original simulations of Delayed Zooming and DLPP, with cumulative-regret curves in Figure 1 and numerical results in Appendix D, Table 1.

after.justification: Section 7 and Appendix D retain the original simulation results for both proposed algorithms, including Figure 1 and Table 1.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Algorithm 2 quarter DLPP's per-ball observation target, from (4 log T + 2 log(2/delta))/r_m^2 to (2 log T + log(2/delta))/(2r_m^2), and increase its pruning threshold from 4r_m to 8r_m. These change stopping and elimination decisions within the existing method. Delayed Zooming is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same triangle and sine reward functions on a one-dimensional domain and the same two-dimensional reward function. Uniform and geometric delays, mean delays of 20 and 50, and delay-free scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Figure 1 and Table 1 retain Delayed Zooming and DLPP, including their delay-free reference settings. BLiN remains discussed as inapplicable rather than experimentally evaluated; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 7 retains the 60,000-round horizon, delta = 0.01, cumulative-regret metric, and reward/delay configurations. The revised DLPP thresholds change the method, but no separate revision to the simulation protocol or additional evaluation is reported.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same comparisons across delay distributions, delay magnitudes, and reward functions. No ablation, sensitivity study, robustness test, or other supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report average cumulative regret over 30 independent trials, without adding empirical confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed information. The changed probability guarantee in Theorem 3 is a theoretical revision.

E6.justification: Figure 1's curves and all 36 numerical entries in Table 1 are unchanged. For example, DLPP's triangle-reward regret with uniform delays of mean 50 remains 326.71. No updated empirical results are reported for the revised DLPP thresholds.

T1.justification: Theorem 3 changes its success probability from 1-delta to 1-2delta, matching Appendix B's union bound. Lemma 11 changes the spatial-error term from r_m to 2r_m, and Lemma 16 doubles the gap bound from 8r_(m-1) to 16r_(m-1), with related derivation edits. The asymptotic regret rates and lower-bound argument remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: introducing delayed Lipschitz bandits, proposing algorithms for bounded and unbounded delays, establishing nearly matching regret bounds, and demonstrating empirical effectiveness.

C2.justification: Section 4 corrects the description of Theorem 1's penalty from expected delay to maximum delay and qualifies the never-missing-feedback statement to rounds before T-tau_max. The empirical interpretations and stated limitation concerning unbounded delays remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D revises DLPP's noise-scaled observation-threshold formula to match the quarter-sized target in Algorithm 2. Other implementation guidance is retained, without new code, data-access, or hardware information.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds references to Qin and Russo (2022), Schlisselberg et al. (2025), Wu and Wager (2022), and McDonald et al. (2023). It also replaces the BOLD/QPM-D characterization of Joulani et al. with partial monitoring. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section sequence are retained. Changes include brief clarifications, covering-number notation, author-year citations, an updated author affiliation, and a new acknowledgements section; there is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted into the ICLR template, changing text-block width, title and author arrangement, recurring headers, heading styles, and equation and algorithm wrapping. Figure 1 is rescaled, and Table 1 moves to a separate final page. Their scientific content and display structure are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects the ball-diameter term in Lemma 11 and aligns Theorem 3's probability guarantee with Appendix B, improving local mathematical precision. The gain is limited: empirical evidence is unchanged, and Appendix B.2 still uses the old phase-regret coefficient despite the doubled bound in Lemma 16.
